sources.title: ASP.NET Core SignalR configuration
sources.finding: Stateful reconnect is opt-in on both server and client and can buffer/replay messages. P1 deliberately does not configure stateful reconnect, replay, retention, or client retry behavior; authoritative recovery remains a BFF/API/read-model read.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core SignalR JavaScript client
sources.finding: Automatic reconnect is opt-in, does not retry an initial start failure, and may establish a new server connection. The reusable foundation therefore has no client recovery contract and requires later clients to re-establish authorized scope and resynchronize authoritatively.

sources.title: SignalR authentication and authorization
sources.finding: Hub authentication and authorization must be explicitly configured. P1 maps only through an authenticated technical policy and delegates server-side audience/resource resolution to the authenticated BFF/domain scope; no client-selected subscription is accepted.

sources.title: Security considerations in ASP.NET Core SignalR
sources.finding: Browser SignalR needs origin, token, logging, and transport controls. The foundation requires named browser-origin and rate-limit policies at mapping time, uses the BFF authenticated browser boundary, and permits no sensitive payload fields.

sources.title: ASP.NET Core SignalR Redis backplane
sources.finding: Redis is a scale-out delivery backplane, not business state. P1 does not configure it; it can be added only when a multi-node Tunner web host needs scale-out.

decision: Existing ADR-0004 and ADR-0002 already select SignalR for Tunner-owned browser realtime and Redis only for optional non-authoritative scale-out. P1 implements a reusable technical foundation only: authenticated policy-gated connection mapping, server-derived audience resolution, payload-minimal resynchronization hints, and explicit browser-boundary/rate-limit hooks. No Product-facing SignalR, domain event category, resource subscription API, client retry/replay policy, or business authority is introduced.
limitations: This evidence does not authorize identity/session implementation, User/Admin BFF host exposure, domain resource-policy semantics, client UX, reconnect timing, replay retention, Product behavior, provider usage, deployment, or release behavior.
Realtime is never an authority for mutation, entitlement, consistency, finality, audit, financial, provider, or owner-domain decisions.
